The [[Mumbai Central]] Railway station, was also built by them at a cost of {{INR}}1.6 [[crore]]. The company was commended for completing the work within 21 months. In 1936, Shapoorji Pallonji bought F.E. Dinshaw and Co. after the death of its promoter. F.E. Dinshaw was an established finance firm that had high-profile dealings such as arranging a loan from the [[Maharaja of Gwalior]] for [[Tata Steel]] (then TISCO) in 1924 and merging local cement companies to form [[ACC Limited|ACC Cement]] in 1936.{{cite book|last=Markovits|first=Claude|title=Indian Business and Nationalist Politics 1931-39: The Indigenous Capitalist Class and the Rise of the Congress Party|year=2002|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=0521016827|pages=208}} F.E. Dinshaw and Co. also had a 12.5% stake in [[Tata Sons]], which came to Shapoorji Pallonji. Shapoorji Pallonji's stake in Tata Sons increased to 18.37% after the latter's [[rights issue]] in 1996.{{cite news |title=SP Group's exit from Tata Group: Who can buy its stake, and how |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/explained-the-impending-exit-of-shapoorji-pallonji-from-tata-6606746/ |access-date=28 September 2024 |work=The Indian Express |date=23 September 2020 |language=en}} In 2001–02, Shapoorji Pallonji took over Forbes Gokak (now [[Forbes & Company Ltd]]) from the [[Tata Group]] after winning a takeover battle with the Pawankumar Sanwarmal Group.{{cite news|title=Sanwarmal exits Forbes, sells to Shapoorji|url=http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2002-01-24/india-business/27133787_1_pallonji-forbes-gokak-pawankumar-group|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130103110504/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2002-01-24/india-business/27133787_1_pallonji-forbes-gokak-pawankumar-group|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 January 2013|access-date=20 March 2012|newspaper=[[The Times of India]]|date=24 January 2002}} In recent years, it has built the [[Barakhamba Road (Delhi Metro)|Barakhamba Underground Station]] in Delhi and [[Providence Stadium]] in [[Guyana]]. After the [[2008 Mumbai attacks]], the company was involved in the repairs and renovation of [[Taj Mahal Palace & Tower]] that was severely damaged by the attack.{{cite news|title='Taj repair costs to be lower than insurance cover'|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/todays-paper/article1644432.ece?ref=archive|access-date=20 March 2012|newspaper=[[The Hindu Business Line]]|date=22 December 2008}} In 2010, it built India's tallest building of the time, [[The Imperial (Mumbai)|The Imperial]], a residential tower in Mumbai. has also had a brief involvement with [[Bollywood]]. Released in 1960, [[K. Asif]]'s ''[[Mughal-e-Azam]]'' was funded by the group with a budget of {{INR}} 1.5 crore, which made it the most expensive Bollywood film till then and a record it held for many years. More than four decades later, the group funded a digital remastering of the film at a budget of {{INR}}5 crore, which was released on 12 November 2004. Shapoor Mistry, grandson of Shapoorji Pallonji Mistry, thought it a fitting tribute to complete his grandfather's unfinished dream of colourising the film, especially as the original was produced by his grandfather. In 2016, Shapoorji Pallonji Group, in association with the [[National Centre for the Performing Arts (India)]], co-produced ''[[Mughal-e-Azam (musical)|Mughal-e-Azam]]'', a [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]]-style [[Musical theatre|musical]] directed by [[Feroz Abbas Khan]], and based on the 1960 Bollywood film ''Mughal-e-Azam''.{{Cite news|url=https://www.livemint.com/Leisure/6Utc4pumyKSv7G0Mh9hZQO/MughaleAzam-now-a-stage-musical.html|title=Mughal-e-Azam, now a stage musical|last=Phukan|first=Vikram|date=24 October 2016|work=Live Mint| access-date=22 May 2018}} ==Key people== {{Distinguish|Shapoorji Mistry}} Shapoor Mistry is an Indian businessman who inherited the group in December 2012, succeeding his brother [[Cyrus Mistry]], who left to lead the [[Tata Group]].{{cite web |last1=Raghunathan |first1=Anu |title=The Mistry Family's Double Tragedy Leaves A Vacuum At The Shapoorji Pallonji Group |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/anuraghunathan/2022/10/12/the-mistry-familys-double-tragedy-leaves-a-vacuum-at-the-shapoorji-pallonji-group/?sh=7a76aa77f665 |website=Forbes |access-date=1 March 2024 |language=en}}{{cite news |title=Cyrus Mistry Death: Who Controls $30-Billion Shapoorji Pallonji Group? Shapoorji Pallonji & Company Private Limited (SPCPL), trading as Shapoorji Pallonji Group, is an Indian conglomerate headquartered in Mumbai. Its primary business interests include construction and engineering, infrastructure, real estate, energy, and textiles, among others. The company was headed by a grandson of founder Pallonji Mistry, also named Pallonji Mistry, until 2012, when he announced his retirement and the succession of his son, Shapoor Mistry.
Shapoorji Pallonji is regarded as "one of India's most valuable private enterprises". The Shapoorji Pallonji Group has three listed companies–Afcons Infrastructure, Forbes & Company Ltd, and Gokak Textiles.
The company is known for building some of Mumbai's landmarks around the Fort area, including the Hong Kong Bank, Grindlays Bank, Standard Chartered Bank and Reserve Bank of India building, Bombay Stock Exchange building and Taj Intercontinental. Apart from these, the company has built Al Alam Palace for the Sultan of Oman in 1972. Other notable projects include The Imperial in Mumbai, Jumeirah Lake Towers in Dubai and Ebene Cyber City in Mauritius.
